analysis: What changed vs the 5:00 AM brief: the tech-led bounce faded after the 8:30 AM ET data. At the 7:00 AM ET update S&P futures were +0.23% and Nasdaq 100 +0.65%; after retail sales printed, Dow futures slipped to -0.9%, S&P 500 -0.2% and Nasdaq 100 +0.2%. The data itself was fine — headline +0.2% in line, core +0.6% vs +0.4% expected — so the fade is positioning, not a consumer scare: with a December hike ~97% priced, strong spending cuts both ways. The morning's fresh company news is Nvidia's 13F (filed Monday evening): a 25% Intel trim that sent Intel -3.3% premarket, Nokia cut 56%, SpaceX added and now Nvidia's largest disclosed holding — but the snapshot is September 30, so it says nothing about tonight's quarter. Microsoft's preliminary outage report is now public (July gateway bug, 80%+ of servers unresponsive at the low point), and the HN thread is active this morning. Home Depot's call starts at 9:00 AM ET with shares -1.9% on a disappointing outlook; Disney's call is in progress, with a dividend raised by a third as the new detail and the 53rd week flattering the beat. China ADRs (JD -3.28%, BABA -3.20%) are weak after soft October China data. Signal vs noise: retail sales and the 13F are real but second-order — everything still funnels into Nvidia after the close (~4:20 PM ET, call 5:00 PM ET, ~8.5% move priced) and the read on whether AI demand and guidance hold after Monday's chip rout, which was triggered by the new Commerce Department licensing rule for AI chips going to data centers in five countries.

headlines.headline: October retail sales rose 0.2% MoM, matching consensus, after an unrevised 0.8% September surge; ex-auto and gas sales +0.5% vs +0.3% expected and core (control group) +0.6% vs +0.4% expected (Census Bureau, 8:30 AM ET). After the release, Dow futures slipped to -0.9%, S&P 500 -0.2%, Nasdaq 100 +0.2% — the early tech-led bounce (S&P +0.23%, Nasdaq +0.65% at 7:00 AM ET) faded into the open.
headlines.why_it_matters: An in-line headline with a firmer core keeps the consumer story intact, but futures fading after the print shows positioning into Nvidia, not the data, is driving the tape — and with a December hike ~97% priced, strong spending cuts both ways.

headlines.headline: Nvidia's 13F (filed Mon Nov 16, ~5:40 PM ET) shows it cut its Intel stake 25% in Q3 (161.1M shares vs 214.8M), cut Nokia 56% and Synopsys 10%, and added 6.3% to SpaceX — now its largest disclosed holding at $19.68B vs Intel's $19.37B. Total disclosed holdings fell to $48.33B from $63.44B. Intel fell ~3.3% premarket on the news; Nvidia held its premarket gain (+0.81% to +1.19%).
headlines.why_it_matters: A 25% Intel trim the night before earnings reads as portfolio housekeeping, but Intel's -3.3% premarket drop shows how every Nvidia move is being repriced — and the filing is a September 30 snapshot, so it says nothing about tonight's quarter.

headlines.headline: Microsoft's preliminary post-incident report (published Nov 15-16) blames last Thursday's global Outlook/Microsoft 365 outage on a latent software defect introduced in a July fix to its networking gateway servers, triggered when a Teams failover added load while ~14% of gateway capacity was already offline; more than 80% of servers were unresponsive at the low point. Service was restored Nov 14; the final report is due Nov 20. MSFT -0.29% premarket.
headlines.why_it_matters: The root cause is now public and contained — a self-inflicted bug, not an attack — but the report leaves open how a defect shipped in July ran undetected for months, which is the reputational question for enterprise customers.

headlines.headline: Home Depot shares fell ~1.9% premarket after the Q3 print: sales of $43.4B (+4.9%) beat, but profit narrowly missed estimates and the outlook (fiscal 2026 sales growth ~4.5%) disappointed investors, per Investopedia. Finance chief Richard McPhail becomes CEO effective Nov 23; Ted Decker steps back to chair after a medical leave since August. Earnings call at 9:00 AM ET.
headlines.why_it_matters: A beat on sales is being ignored — the market is trading the outlook and the leadership transition, and the call will be watched for transition commentary.

headlines.headline: Disney raised its annual dividend by a third alongside the fiscal Q4 beat (adjusted EPS $1.77 vs $1.67 expected, revenue $25.9B, +16%), but the quarter contained a 53rd week that added ~$1.6B of revenue — flattering the growth. Experiences operating income +20% to $2.25B; streaming revenue +19% to $6.1B. Shares were -1.85% to -2.51% premarket after the initial pop; the call is in progress (8:30 AM ET).
headlines.why_it_matters: The dividend hike and cost-savings plan are real positives, but the premarket fade after the pop — and the 53rd-week caveat — show the market is trading Nvidia and macro today, not earnings beats.

headlines.headline: China ADRs are weak after soft October China data: JD.com -3.28%, Alibaba -3.20% premarket. China's industrial output rose 4.8% YoY vs 5.3% expected and retail sales just 0.4% vs 0.8% expected, despite the national holiday and Singles Day.
headlines.why_it_matters: Weak China demand is a headwind for global growth names and keeps the risk-off tone in place outside the Nvidia trade.
